column1: # --- the END marker cuts a forward collection short ----------------------
# `;` is the punctuation spelling of `end` (REFERENCE.md:415); the corpus
# uses the punctuation so a row can still name a WORD called end. A pending
# forward word fires with whatever it has collected, which for these
# fixtures is never enough — the value of the rows is that the marker
# REACHES the word rather than being dropped, and that a bare `;` with no
# pending marker is silently dropped instead of erroring.
# --- the WORD `end` is not the end MARKER -------------------------------
# `;` is the marker (above); the bare word `end` is an ordinary name, and
# core defines no word by it. These rows were 9 rows of divergent.tsv until
# core/ts's isEnd stopped treating a Word named "end" as the marker — a
# fallback left over from the legacy fixture tokenizer that Go's IsEnd never
# had, and that made `run end 1` the value 1 here against Go's error.
# `Word` names the lattice branch, and its literal shares that branch's
# vType. core/ts's isWord() tested the vType ALONE, so stepWord resolved
# the name, wrote the literal back to the same slot, and the step loop
# re-entered stepWord on it — ending in an UNCODED `AsWord: not a word
# value` that escaped the BoruError taxonomy entirely. isWord() now
# requires word DATA, which is what separates a word from its type.
# REFERENCE.md:364 lists "another function word" as a forward-collection
# barrier, and design/STRICT-FORWARD-BARRIER.0.md makes it uniform: a
# parked forward that cannot commit with the args it already holds is
# STRANDED, a signature_error, not a wait-through. The rule does not ask
# how many args the boundary word collects — a nullary `depthq` and a
# The GROUPED spelling is what fires the outer word, and that contrast is
# the whole point of the rule: `boomq ( negq 5 )` raises fixture_boom
# while `boomq negq 5` refuses. core/ts had no such rule and waited
# through — 30 rows of divergent.tsv until it did.
# --- a VOID paren group in the forward window ---------------------------
# A `( )` that resolves to nothing cannot fill the slot it sits in, so it
# STOPS forward collection: the word falls back to stack form where a
# stack operand can supply the arg, and raises no_value_error where none
# can. core/ts scanned PAST the void instead, letting the next group slide
# into the empty slot — `7 8 addq ( ) ( 5 )` was `7 13` here against Go's
# `15 5`, the one divergence in the whole ledger that produced a wrong
# NUMBER rather than a wrong error.
# The stop exposed a second defect it had been hiding: preEvalParens
# derived the group's result count as `length - (before - 1)`, arithmetic
# that only holds for a two-token group and goes negative for every longer
# one. evalParenAt now returns the count.
# --- an UNDEFINED word in the forward window ----------------------------
# A name nothing binds is reported, not swallowed. Go's forward PLAN
# resolves an unknown word to an Atom, but the plan is SPECULATIVE — the
# token is still stepped, and stepping it raises. core/ts consumed it as
# data at an `Any` slot instead, so `boomq zzz` fired boomq. Any Word that
# survives resolution now DEFERS the dispatch, which is what lets the
# engine reach it: refusing outright looks equivalent and is not, because
# `def inc fn […]` needs its keyword to reach its slot.
# --- builtin type names: the LEAF form and the PATH form ----------------
# Go's ResolveBuiltinTypeName tries the user-facing leaf table first and
# then the full path (core/go/resolve.go:23); core/ts had only the leaf
# half. The path arm admits only paths the builtin table declares, so an
# invented one stays undefined rather than minting a type.
